```{r root, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = rstudioapi::getActiveProject())
```

# Aim

Identify which genera of the reef BCM communities change in abundance with the environmental variables (DIN, PO₄³⁻, temperature, chl-a), and which of those responses are stable.

Workflow:

1. Genus-level community from read counts; ASVs without a genus are grouped at their lowest assigned rank.
2. Null GLLVMs (no predictors) with 0, 1 and 2 latent variables.
3. GLLVM with 2 latent variables + DIN + PO₄³⁻ + temperature + chl-a.
4. Coefficients of all genera (full coefficient plot).
5. Stability workflow: numerical stability, significance (BH-adjusted by default, see `sig_rule`), effect size, second starting value, leave-one-site-out refits, 1 and 3 latent variables, and per-genus GLMMs.
6. Final coefficient plot of the genera with a robust response.

Models are saved in `outputs/models/reefs/6c/` and loaded from there; a missing model is fitted (this can take hours). Set `refit_models <- TRUE` to refit everything. File names include the data settings, so changing a setting never loads a model fitted on other data.

Outputs: `figures/6c.gllvm_genus_responses/F<n>_<name>.pdf` and `outputs/6c.gllvm_genus_responses/T<n>_<name>.docx` (+ `.csv`).

```{r setup, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
rm(packages_used, missing_pkgs)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE,

fig_dir   <- "figures/6c.gllvm_genus_responses"
```

## Settings

```{r settings}
refit_models <- FALSE   # TRUE = refit every model (hours)

# ---- Data ----
unassigned_grouping <- "lowest_rank"  # "lowest_rank": ASVs without a genus grouped at their lowest assigned rank
                                      # "pooled": all of them in one "Unidentified genus" column
                                      # "drop": excluded
min_prev  <- 0.20   # taxon present (>= 1 read) in at least this proportion of mats
min_reads <- 100    # and with at least this many reads in total

# ---- Models ----
use_offset  <- TRUE                                   # log(total filtered reads per mat) as offset
n_init      <- 3                                      # starting values per fit (best is kept)
env_formula <- ~ DIN + mean.PO4 + temperature + chla  # predictors (scaled)

# ---- Coefficient filters ----
sig_rule     <- "ci"  # "p_adj": BH-adjusted p < 0.05 (corrected for the number of taxa)
                         # "ci":    95% Wald CI excludes 0 (= raw p < 0.05; gllvm coefplot convention)
p_adj_method <- "BH"     # within each predictor, as in scripts 2 and 3
max_abs_est  <- 10       # |coefficient| >= 10 (> 22,000-fold per SD) = numerically unstable
max_se       <- 3        # SE >= 3 = numerically unstable
min_effect   <- log(2)   # |coefficient| > log(2): at least a two-fold change per SD

# ---- Stability checks (each adds model fits; a check that is not run is not required) ----
run_seed_check <- TRUE   # 1 extra fit: second starting value
run_loso       <- TRUE   # 8 extra fits: leave one site out
loso_min       <- 8      # refits (of 8) in which the sign must be the same
run_lv_check   <- TRUE   # 2 extra fits: 1 and 3 latent variables
run_glmm_check <- TRUE   # one GLMM per genus (fast)

stopifnot(sig_rule %in% c("p_adj", "ci"))
# Significance under the chosen rule (used in every step, including the stability checks)
is_sig <- function(p, p_adj) {
  out <- if (sig_rule == "p_adj") p_adj < 0.05 else p < 0.05
  !is.na(out) & out
}
sig_label <- if (sig_rule == "p_adj") paste0(p_adj_method, "-adjusted p < 0.05") else "95% CI excludes 0"

# Model file tag: data and fit settings that change the model
model_tag <- paste0("_", unassigned_grouping, "_prev", round(100 * min_prev),
                    "_reads", min_reads, if (use_offset) "_offset" else "")
```

## Output helpers

```{r output helpers}
save_fig <- function(plot, name, width = 11, height = 11) {
  ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, paste0(name, ".pdf")), plot = plot,
         device = cairo_pdf, width = width, height = height, units = "in", limitsize = FALSE)
}

save_base_fig <- function(name, draw, width = 11, height = 11) {
  draw()
  cairo_pdf(file.path(fig_dir, paste0(name, ".pdf")), width = width, height = height)
  draw()
  dev.off()
  invisible()
}

save_tab <- function(tables, name) {
  if (is.data.frame(tables)) tables <- setNames(list(tables), name)
  doc <- read_docx()
  for (nm in names(tables)) {
    doc <- body_add_par(doc, nm, style = "Normal")
    doc <- body_add_flextable(doc, autofit(flextable(tables[[nm]])))
    doc <- body_add_par(doc, "")
  }
  print(doc, target = file.path(tab_dir, paste0(name, ".docx")))
  for (nm in names(tables)) {
    suffix <- if (length(tables) > 1) paste0("_", gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", nm)) else ""
    write.csv(tables[[nm]], file.path(tab_dir, paste0(name, suffix, ".csv")), row.names = FALSE)
  }
}

otu_matrix <- function(ps) {
  m <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
  if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) m <- t(m)
  m
}

# Same definition of "unassigned" as in script 2
is_unassigned <- function(x) {
  is.na(x) | x == "" |
    grepl("unknown|unidentified|uncultured|unclassified|metagenome", x, ignore.case = TRUE)
}
```

#--------------------------

# 1. Data

## 1.1 Counts, taxonomy and metadata

GLLVMs need read counts, so the filtered count phyloseq is used (`reef_counts`), not the TSS object of scripts 2 and 3.

```{r data}
reef_counts <- readRDS("data/bcms_filtered_raja2023.rds")

community.counts <- otu_matrix(reef_counts)   # mats x ASVs
if (any(community.counts != round(community.counts)))
  warning("community.counts contains non-integer values: negative binomial models need counts")

tax_df <- as.data.frame(as(tax_table(reef_counts), "matrix")) %>%
  rownames_to_column("ASV")

env <- as(sample_data(reef_counts), "data.frame") %>% filter(!is.na(site))
stopifnot(all(unique(env$site) %in% names(site_labels)))
env <- env %>% mutate(site = factor(site_labels[site], levels = site_levels))
rownames(env) <- env$sample_id

env_scaled <- read.csv("data/environmental_scaled_filtered.csv", row.names = 1)
stopifnot(all(names(env_vars) %in% colnames(env_scaled)))
```

## 1.2 Genus-level grouping

Ranks reported as uncultured, unidentified, etc. are treated as unassigned, so that e.g. all "uncultured" genera of different families are not merged into one taxon.

With `unassigned_grouping = "lowest_rank"`, an ASV without a genus is grouped at its lowest assigned rank, e.g. "Rhodobacteraceae (unidentified genus)". Taxa get a short internal ID (`tax001`, ...) for the models; their labels are used in tables and plots.

```{r taxon grouping}
ranks <- c("Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus")

tax_lab <- tax_df %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(ranks), ~ ifelse(is_unassigned(.x), NA_character_, .x)),
         genus_assigned = !is.na(Genus),
         lowest = case_when(
           !is.na(Genus)  ~ Genus,
           !is.na(Family) ~ paste0(Family, " (unidentified genus)"),
           !is.na(Order)  ~ paste0(Order,  " (unidentified family)"),
           !is.na(Class)  ~ paste0(Class,  " (unidentified order)"),
           !is.na(Phylum) ~ paste0(Phylum, " (unidentified class)"),
           TRUE           ~ "Unidentified"),
         taxon = case_when(
           unassigned_grouping == "lowest_rank" ~ lowest,
           unassigned_grouping == "pooled"      ~ ifelse(genus_assigned, Genus, "Unidentified genus"),
           unassigned_grouping == "drop"        ~ ifelse(genus_assigned, Genus, NA_character_)))

# Sum ASV counts per taxon
asv_taxon <- tax_lab$taxon[match(colnames(community.counts), tax_lab$ASV)]
keep_asv  <- !is.na(asv_taxon)
Y_all     <- t(rowsum(t(community.counts[, keep_asv, drop = FALSE]), group = asv_taxon[keep_asv]))
Y_all     <- Y_all[rowSums(Y_all) > 0, , drop = FALSE]

# Prevalence and read filter
keep_taxa <- colMeans(Y_all >= 1) >= min_prev & colSums(Y_all) >= min_reads
Y_taxa    <- Y_all[, keep_taxa, drop = FALSE]

# Taxon information: ID, label, phylum (most common phylum of its ASVs), number of ASVs
taxon_info <- tax_lab %>%
  filter(taxon %in% colnames(Y_taxa), ASV %in% colnames(community.counts)) %>%
  group_by(taxon) %>%
  summarise(Phylum = {
              ph <- Phylum[!is.na(Phylum)]
              if (length(ph) == 0) "Unidentified" else names(sort(table(ph), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
            },
            genus_assigned = all(genus_assigned),
            n_ASV = n(),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(taxon) %>%
  mutate(taxon_id = sprintf("tax%03d", row_number()),
                  missing_rank = sub("^.* \\(unidentified (genus|family|order|class)\\)$", "\\1", taxon),
         group_name   = sub(" \\(unidentified (genus|family|order|class)\\)$", "", taxon),
         group_rank   = unname(c(genus = "family", family = "order",
                                 order = "class", class = "phylum")[missing_rank]),
         label_md = case_when(
           genus_assigned    ~ paste0("<i>", taxon, "</i>"),
           is.na(group_rank) ~ taxon,
           TRUE              ~ paste0("Unclassified <i>", group_name, "</i> (", group_rank, ")"))) %>%
  select(-missing_rank, -group_name)

colnames(Y_taxa) <- taxon_info$taxon_id[match(colnames(Y_taxa), taxon_info$taxon)]
```

## 1.3 Model data

```{r model data}
# Y, X and study design with the same mats in the same order
prep_gllvm <- function(Y, X_source = env_scaled) {
  Y   <- as.matrix(Y)
  Y   <- Y[rowSums(Y) > 0, , drop = FALSE]
  ids <- Reduce(intersect, list(rownames(Y), rownames(X_source), rownames(env)))
  dropped <- setdiff(rownames(Y), ids)
  if (length(dropped) > 0) message("Mats dropped (missing predictors or metadata): ", paste(dropped, collapse = ", "))
  Y <- Y[ids, , drop = FALSE]
  Y <- Y[, colSums(Y) > 0, drop = FALSE]
  X      <- X_source[ids, all.vars(env_formula), drop = FALSE]
  design <- env[ids, "site", drop = FALSE]
  stopifnot(identical(rownames(Y), rownames(X)), identical(rownames(Y), rownames(design)),
            !anyNA(design$site), !anyNA(X))
  list(Y = Y, X = X, design = design)
}

d_genus <- prep_gllvm(Y_taxa)

data_summary <- tibble(
  mats                       = nrow(d_genus$Y),
  sites                      = n_distinct(d_genus$design$site),
  ASVs                       = ncol(community.counts),
  taxa_before_filter         = ncol(Y_all),
  taxa_modelled              = ncol(d_genus$Y),
  of_which_unidentified_genus = sum(!taxon_info$genus_assigned),
  reads_modelled_pct         = round(100 * sum(d_genus$Y) / sum(community.counts[rownames(d_genus$Y), ]), 1),
  zero_cells_pct             = round(100 * mean(d_genus$Y == 0), 1),
  unassigned_grouping        = unassigned_grouping,
  min_prevalence             = min_prev,
  min_reads                  = min_reads)
data_summary

save_tab(data_summary, "T1_data_summary")
```

## 1.4 Data exploration

```{r mean variance}
p_mv <- data.frame(mean = colMeans(d_genus$Y), var = apply(d_genus$Y, 2, var)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(mean, var)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +   # Poisson: variance = mean
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Mean count", y = "Variance", title = "Mean-variance relationship of the modelled taxa") +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
p_mv
save_fig(p_mv, "F1_mean_variance", width = 6, height = 6)
```

Variance increasing much faster than the mean (points far above the 1:1 line) indicates overdispersion, supporting the negative binomial distribution.

# 2. Model helpers

```{r model helpers}
# Negative binomial GLLVM with a random site intercept and (optionally) a sequencing-depth offset.
# The offset uses the total filtered reads of each mat (all ASVs), not only the modelled taxa.
fit_nb <- function(d, formula = NULL, num.lv = 2, sd.errors = TRUE, n.init = n_init, seed = 123) {
  args <- list(y = d$Y, studyDesign = d$design, family = "negative.binomial",
               row.eff = ~(1 | site), num.lv = num.lv, sd.errors = sd.errors,
               n.init = n.init, seed = seed)
  if (use_offset) {
    lib_size    <- rowSums(community.counts)[rownames(d$Y)]
    args$offset <- matrix(log(lib_size), nrow = nrow(d$Y), ncol = ncol(d$Y))
  }
  if (!is.null(formula)) {
    args$X       <- d$X
    args$formula <- formula
  }
  do.call(gllvm, args)
}

# Load a saved model, or fit and save it
fit_or_load <- function(name, fit_expr) {
  path <- file.path(model_dir, paste0(name, model_tag, ".rds"))
  if (!refit_models && file.exists(path)) return(readRDS(path))
  message("Fitting ", name, " ...")
  t0 <- Sys.time()
  m  <- fit_expr
  message(name, " fitted in ", format(round(Sys.time() - t0, 1)))
  saveRDS(m, path)
  gc()
  m
}

aicc_safe <- function(m) tryCatch(AICc(m), error = function(e)
  tryCatch(AICc.gllvm(m), error = function(e) NA_real_))

aic_table <- function(models) {
  tibble(Model     = names(models),
         n_LV      = sapply(models, function(m) m$num.lv),
         converged = sapply(models, function(m) isTRUE(m$convergence)),
         logLik    = sapply(models, function(m) as.numeric(logLik(m))),
         df        = sapply(models, function(m) attr(logLik(m), "df")),
         AIC       = sapply(models, AIC),
         AICc      = sapply(models, aicc_safe),
         BIC       = sapply(models, BIC)) %>%
    mutate(dAIC = AIC - min(AIC)) %>%
    arrange(AIC) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2)))
}

# Likelihood-ratio test between nested models with the same number of latent variables
compare_gllvm <- function(reduced, full) {
  if (reduced$num.lv != full$num.lv) warning("Different numbers of latent variables: models are not nested")
  LL_f <- logLik(full); LL_r <- logLik(reduced)
  df   <- attr(LL_f, "df") - attr(LL_r, "df")
  LRT  <- max(0, 2 * (as.numeric(LL_f) - as.numeric(LL_r)))
  tibble(LRT = LRT, df = df, p = pchisq(LRT, df, lower.tail = FALSE))
}

# Coefficients with Wald SE, 95% CI, p and BH-adjusted p (within each predictor)
coef_table <- function(m) {
  est <- m$params$Xcoef
  se  <- m$sd$Xcoef
  if (is.null(se)) stop("Model has no standard errors: fit with sd.errors = TRUE")
  dimnames(se) <- dimnames(est)
  long <- function(x, v) as.data.frame(x) %>% rownames_to_column("taxon_id") %>%
    pivot_longer(-taxon_id, names_to = "Variable", values_to = v)
  long(est, "Estimate") %>%
    left_join(long(se, "SE"), by = c("taxon_id", "Variable")) %>%
    mutate(cilow = Estimate - qnorm(0.975) * SE,
           ciup  = Estimate + qnorm(0.975) * SE,
           p     = 2 * pnorm(-abs(Estimate / SE))) %>%
    group_by(Variable) %>%
    mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p, method = p_adj_method)) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# Estimates only (models fitted without standard errors)
coef_est <- function(m) {
  as.data.frame(m$params$Xcoef) %>% rownames_to_column("taxon_id") %>%
    pivot_longer(-taxon_id, names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Estimate")
}

# Mat scores on the first two latent variables, with raw environmental values
ord_plot <- function(m, colour_var, title) {
  df <- as.data.frame(getLV(m)[, 1:2, drop = FALSE]) %>% setNames(c("LV1", "LV2")) %>%
    rownames_to_column("sample_id") %>%
    left_join(env %>% select(sample_id, site, all_of(names(env_vars))), by = "sample_id")
  ggplot(df, aes(LV1, LV2)) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = .data[[colour_var]], shape = site), size = 3, stroke = 1.1) +
    scale_colour_viridis_c(name = parse(text = env_vars[[colour_var]])) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = shape_sites, name = "Site") +
    labs(x = "Latent variable 1", y = "Latent variable 2", title = title) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid = element_blank())
}
```

#--------------------------

# 3. Null models: number of latent variables

Models without predictors, with 0, 1 and 2 latent variables. Standard errors are not needed to compare them.

```{r null models}
gllvm_null0lv <- fit_or_load("null0lv", fit_nb(d_genus, num.lv = 0, sd.errors = FALSE))
gllvm_null1lv <- fit_or_load("null1lv", fit_nb(d_genus, num.lv = 1, sd.errors = FALSE))
gllvm_null2lv <- fit_or_load("null2lv", fit_nb(d_genus, num.lv = 2, sd.errors = FALSE))
beep(2)

null_models <- list("Null, 0 LV" = gllvm_null0lv,
                    "Null, 1 LV" = gllvm_null1lv,
                    "Null, 2 LV" = gllvm_null2lv)
aic_null <- aic_table(null_models)
aic_null
```

The number of latent variables with the lowest AIC is used for the environmental model (2 LV expected).

## 3.1 Residual diagnostics (null, 2 LV)

Dunn-Smyth residuals against linear predictors (even scatter around 0, no funnel or curve) and normal QQ plot (points along the line).

```{r null residuals, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 6}
save_base_fig("F2_residuals_null2lv", function() {
  par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
  plot(gllvm_null2lv, which = 1:2, var.colors = 1, n.plot = 100)
}, width = 12, height = 6)
```

## 3.2 Unconstrained ordination

Mat scores of the 2-LV null model, coloured by each environmental variable. A colour gradient along an axis suggests the variable is related to the main community patterns.

```{r null ordination}
ord_null <- lapply(setNames(names(env_vars), names(env_vars)), function(v)
  ord_plot(gllvm_null2lv, v, "Unconstrained GLLVM (null, 2 LV)"))
ord_null

for (i in seq_along(ord_null))
  save_fig(ord_null[[i]], paste0("F3", letters[i], "_ordination_null2lv_", names(ord_null)[i]),
           width = 8, height = 8)
```

# 4. Environmental model: 2 LV + DIN + PO₄³⁻ + temperature + chl-a

```{r env model}
gllvm_env <- fit_or_load("env2lv", fit_nb(d_genus, env_formula, num.lv = 2, sd.errors = TRUE))
beep(4)

tibble(converged  = isTRUE(gllvm_env$convergence),
       family     = gllvm_env$family,
       n_LV       = gllvm_env$num.lv,
       mats       = nrow(gllvm_env$y),
       taxa       = ncol(gllvm_env$y),
       predictors = paste(colnames(gllvm_env$params$Xcoef), collapse = ", "),
       offset     = use_offset,
       starts     = n_init)
```

```{r model comparison}

aic_all

  mutate(Comparison = "Environmental model vs null (2 LV)", .before = 1) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))
lrt_env

save_tab(list("AIC" = aic_all, "Likelihood-ratio test" = lrt_env), "T2_model_comparison")
```

#--------------------------

# 5. Coefficients

Each taxon has one coefficient per predictor: the change in its log expected abundance per standard deviation of the predictor, given the other predictors, the site effect, sequencing depth and the latent variables. exp(coefficient) is the fold change per SD.

```{r coefficients}
coef_env <- coef_table(gllvm_env) %>%
  left_join(taxon_info %>% select(taxon_id, taxon, Phylum, genus_assigned, n_ASV), by = "taxon_id") %>%
  mutate(fold_change    = exp(Estimate),
         numerically_ok = !is.na(SE) & abs(Estimate) < max_abs_est & SE < max_se,
         sig_ci         = !is.na(p) & p < 0.05,           # 95% CI excludes 0 (no correction)
         sig_bh         = !is.na(p_adj) & p_adj < 0.05,   # after BH correction
         stat_ok        = is_sig(p, p_adj),               # rule set in sig_rule
         effect_ok      = abs(Estimate) > min_effect)

# How many coefficients are significant without and with the BH correction
sig_comparison <- coef_env %>%
  filter(numerically_ok) %>%
  group_by(Variable) %>%
  summarise(taxa                = n(),
            CI_excludes_0       = sum(sig_ci),
            expected_false_pos  = round(0.05 * n(), 1),   # if no taxon truly responded
            BH_p_adj_below_0.05 = sum(sig_bh),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = names(env_vars))) %>%
  arrange(Variable)
sig_comparison

save_tab(sig_comparison, "T3_significance_CI_vs_BH")
```

`CI_excludes_0` is what most GLLVM papers report (black vs grey in `coefplot()`). `expected_false_pos` is how many of those you would expect by chance alone (5% of the taxa tested) if no taxon responded at all. If `CI_excludes_0` is not clearly larger than that number, most uncorrected "responses" may be false positives. The BH column keeps the expected share of false positives among the significant taxa at 5%.

## 5.1 Coefficient plot function

Layout of the final figure: phylum bar and coloured taxon labels on the left, one panel per predictor, 95% CI.

```{r coef plot function}
phylum_palette <- function(phyla) {
  pal  <- phylum_colors[phyla]
  miss <- is.na(pal)
  if (any(miss)) pal[miss] <- grDevices::hcl.colors(sum(miss), "Dark 3")
  setNames(unname(pal), phyla)
}

coef_panel_plot <- function(cd, title, subtitle = NULL, colour_by = NULL, label_size = 8,
                            x_lab = "Coefficient (95% CI)") {
# Phyla in a fixed order (top to bottom); phyla not listed follow alphabetically, Unidentified last
  phylum_order <- c("Cyanobacteriota", "Proteobacteria", "Bacteroidota", "Planctomycetota",
                    "Verrucomicrobiota", "Myxococcota", "Crenarchaeota", "Actinobacteriota", "Bdellovibrionota")
  present <- unique(as.character(cd$Phylum))
  phyla   <- c(intersect(phylum_order, present),
               sort(setdiff(present, c(phylum_order, "Unidentified"))),
               intersect("Unidentified", present))
  pal   <- phylum_palette(phyla)

  # Taxa grouped by phylum, ordered by mean coefficient within phylum
  ord <- cd %>%
    mutate(Phylum = factor(Phylum, levels = phyla)) %>%
    group_by(taxon_id, Phylum) %>%
    summarise(m = mean(Estimate), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(Phylum, m) %>%
    pull(taxon_id)
  lv <- rev(ord)   # first taxon at the top

  info    <- taxon_info[match(ord, taxon_info$taxon_id), ]
  labs_md <- setNames(paste0("<span style='color:", pal[info$Phylum], "'>", info$label_md, "</span>"), ord)

  # Left: phylum bar with taxon labels
  side <- tibble(taxon_id = factor(ord, levels = lv), Phylum = factor(info$Phylum, levels = phyla))
  p_side <- ggplot(side, aes(x = 1, y = taxon_id, fill = Phylum)) +
    geom_tile(width = 1, height = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal, name = "Phylum", drop = FALSE,
                      guide = guide_legend(ncol = 3, title.position = "top")) +
    scale_y_discrete(limits = lv, labels = labs_md, expand = expansion(add = 0.5)) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_markdown(size = label_size, hjust = 1, margin = margin(r = 4)))

  # Right: coefficients, one panel per predictor
  pd <- cd %>% mutate(taxon_id = factor(taxon_id, levels = lv),
                      Variable = factor(Variable, levels = names(env_vars)))
  p_coef <- ggplot(pd, aes(x = Estimate, y = taxon_id)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed")
  if (is.null(colour_by)) {
    p_coef <- p_coef +
      geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = cilow, xmax = ciup), width = 0, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
      geom_point(size = 2.2, colour = "black")
  } else {
    p_coef <- p_coef +
      geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = cilow, xmax = ciup, colour = .data[[colour_by]]), width = 0, linewidth = 0.5) +
      geom_point(aes(colour = .data[[colour_by]], shape = .data[[colour_by]]),
                 size = 2, fill = "white", stroke = 0.8) +
      scale_colour_manual(values = class_colours, name = NULL) +
      scale_shape_manual(values = class_shapes, name = NULL)
  }
  p_coef <- p_coef +
    scale_y_discrete(limits = lv, expand = expansion(add = 0.5)) +
    facet_grid(~ Variable, drop = FALSE, labeller = as_labeller(env_vars, label_parsed)) +
    labs(x = x_lab, y = NULL) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(axis.text.y      = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.y     = element_blank(),
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey85", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.8),
          strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
          panel.border     = element_rect(colour = "black", linewidth = 1),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

  (p_side | p_coef) +
    plot_layout(widths = c(0.35, 10), guides = "collect") +
    plot_annotation(title = title, subtitle = subtitle,
                    theme = theme(plot.title    = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16),
                                  plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11))) &
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
          legend.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"))
}
```

## 5.2 Full coefficient plot (all taxa)

All modelled taxa. Black: significant (rule in `sig_rule`) with at least a two-fold change per SD; grey: not. Numerically unstable coefficients are left out (their number is given in the subtitle).

```{r full coef plot data}
coef_full_plot_df <- coef_env %>%
  filter(numerically_ok) %>%
  mutate(class = ifelse(stat_ok & effect_ok, "Significant", "Not significant"),
         class = factor(class, levels = names(class_colours)))

n_unstable <- sum(!coef_env$numerically_ok)

# Figure size grows with the number of taxa (used for both the html and the pdf)
full_w <- 14
full_h <- max(10, 0.16 * n_distinct(coef_full_plot_df$taxon_id) + 4)
```

```{r full coef plot, fig.width = full_w, fig.height = full_h}
coef_full_plot <- coef_panel_plot(
  coef_full_plot_df,
  title     = "Reef - all genera: GLLVM coefficients",
  subtitle  = paste0(n_distinct(coef_full_plot_df$taxon_id), " taxa; ",
                     n_unstable, " numerically unstable coefficients not shown"),
  colour_by = "class", label_size = 6)
print(coef_full_plot)

save_fig(coef_full_plot, "F6_coefficients_all_taxa", width = full_w, height = full_h)
```

## 5.3 Genera with a significant response to at least one variable

Taxa with at least one significant coefficient (rule in `sig_rule`, numerically stable), before the effect-size filter and the stability checks. All four coefficients of these taxa are shown: black = significant, grey = not, so you can see whether a taxon responds to one variable or to several.

```{r sig any plot data}
sig_any_taxa <- coef_env %>%
  filter(numerically_ok, stat_ok) %>%
  distinct(taxon_id) %>%
  pull(taxon_id)

coef_sig_any_df <- coef_env %>%
  filter(taxon_id %in% sig_any_taxa, numerically_ok) %>%
  mutate(class = factor(ifelse(stat_ok, "Significant", "Not significant"),
                        levels = names(class_colours)))

sig_any_w <- 13
sig_any_h <- max(8, 0.25 * length(sig_any_taxa) + 4)
```

```{r sig any plot, fig.width = sig_any_w, fig.height = sig_any_h}
  message("No taxon has a significant coefficient with sig_rule = '", sig_rule, "'.")
} else {
  coef_sig_any_plot <- coef_panel_plot(
    coef_sig_any_df,
    title     = "Reef - All Genera (Filtered by prevalence and significant at any variable)",
    subtitle  = paste0(length(sig_any_taxa), " taxa with ", sig_label,
                       " for at least one variable (before effect-size and stability filters)"),
    colour_by = "class", label_size = 8, x_lab = "Coefficient")
  print(coef_sig_any_plot)

  save_fig(coef_sig_any_plot, "F7_coefficients_significant_any_variable",
           width = sig_any_w, height = sig_any_h)
}
```

#--------------------------

# 6. Stability workflow

A coefficient is classed as:

- **Robust**: numerically stable, significant (rule in `sig_rule`), at least a two-fold change per SD, and passing every stability check that was run (second starting value, leave-one-site-out, 1 and 3 LV, per-genus GLMM);
- **Supported**: numerically stable, significant and with a sufficient effect, but failing one of the stability checks;
- **Not supported**: numerically unstable, not significant, or a negligible effect.

## 6.1 Second starting value

The model is refitted from a different starting value (one start). If both fits reach the same log-likelihood and nearly identical coefficients, the main fit is not stuck in a local optimum.

```{r seed check, eval = run_seed_check}
gllvm_env_seed2 <- fit_or_load("env2lv_seed2",
                               fit_nb(d_genus, env_formula, sd.errors = FALSE, n.init = 1, seed = 2))

seed_check <- tibble(
  logLik_main  = as.numeric(logLik(gllvm_env)),
  logLik_seed2 = as.numeric(logLik(gllvm_env_seed2)),
  coef_cor     = cor(as.vector(gllvm_env$params$Xcoef), as.vector(gllvm_env_seed2$params$Xcoef)),
  max_abs_diff = max(abs(gllvm_env$params$Xcoef - gllvm_env_seed2$params$Xcoef))) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ round(.x, 3)))
seed_check
```

A coefficient correlation below ~0.95, or a clearly higher log-likelihood for the second fit, means the main model should be refitted with more starting values (`n_init`).

## 6.2 Leave-one-site-out

The environmental model is refitted 8 times, each time without one site (without standard errors, one start). A response that changes sign when one site is removed depends on that site.

```{r loso, eval = run_loso}
subset_d <- function(d, keep) {
  Y <- d$Y[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  Y <- Y[, colSums(Y) > 0, drop = FALSE]
  list(Y = Y, X = d$X[keep, , drop = FALSE], design = droplevels(d$design[keep, , drop = FALSE]))
}

sites_in_data <- levels(droplevels(d_genus$design$site))

loso_est <- lapply(sites_in_data, function(s) {
  m <- fit_or_load(paste0("env2lv_loso_", gsub("[^A-Za-z]", "", s)),
                   fit_nb(subset_d(d_genus, d_genus$design$site != s), env_formula,
                          sd.errors = FALSE, n.init = 1))
  coef_est(m) %>% rename(est_loso = Estimate) %>% mutate(left_out = s)
}) %>% bind_rows()
beep(4)

loso_summary <- coef_env %>%
  select(taxon_id, Variable, Estimate) %>%
  left_join(loso_est, by = c("taxon_id", "Variable")) %>%
  group_by(taxon_id, Variable) %>%
  summarise(loso_n         = sum(!is.na(est_loso)),
            loso_same_sign = sum(sign(est_loso) == sign(first(Estimate)), na.rm = TRUE),
            loso_min_est   = suppressWarnings(min(est_loso, na.rm = TRUE)),
            loso_max_est   = suppressWarnings(max(est_loso, na.rm = TRUE)),
            loso_flip_site = paste(left_out[!is.na(est_loso) & sign(est_loso) != sign(first(Estimate))],
                                   collapse = ", "),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(loso_ok = loso_same_sign >= loso_min)
```

## 6.3 Number of latent variables

The environmental model refitted with 1 and 3 latent variables. A robust response keeps its sign and stays significant.

```{r lv check, eval = run_lv_check}
lv_check <- lapply(c(1, 3), function(k) {
  m <- fit_or_load(paste0("env", k, "lv"), fit_nb(d_genus, env_formula, num.lv = k, sd.errors = TRUE))
  coef_table(m) %>% transmute(taxon_id, Variable, est_k = Estimate, p_k = p, p_adj_k = p_adj, k = k)
}) %>% bind_rows() %>%
  left_join(coef_env %>% select(taxon_id, Variable, Estimate), by = c("taxon_id", "Variable")) %>%
  group_by(taxon_id, Variable) %>%
  summarise(lv_ok = all(sign(est_k) == sign(Estimate) & is_sig(p_k, p_adj_k), na.rm = FALSE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(lv_ok = ifelse(is.na(lv_ok), FALSE, lv_ok))
beep(4)
```

## 6.4 Per-genus GLMMs

Each taxon fitted separately with a negative binomial GLMM (`glmmTMB`): same predictors, site random intercept and offset, but without latent variables. A robust response has the same sign and is significant (same rule; BH within each predictor) in this independent model.

```{r glmm check, eval = run_glmm_check}
glmm_data <- data.frame(d_genus$X, site = d_genus$design$site,
                        log_lib = log(rowSums(community.counts)[rownames(d_genus$Y)]))
glmm_formula <- reformulate(c(all.vars(env_formula), if (use_offset) "offset(log_lib)", "(1 | site)"),
                            response = "y")

glmm_check <- lapply(colnames(d_genus$Y), function(tx) {
  dat   <- glmm_data
  dat$y <- d_genus$Y[, tx]
  fit <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(glmmTMB(glmm_formula, data = dat, family = nbinom2)),
                  error = function(e) NULL)
  cf  <- if (is.null(fit)) NULL else tryCatch(summary(fit)$coefficients$cond, error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(cf)) return(NULL)
  cf <- cf[rownames(cf) %in% all.vars(env_formula), , drop = FALSE]
  tibble(taxon_id = tx, Variable = rownames(cf), est_glmm = cf[, 1], p_glmm = cf[, 4])
}) %>% bind_rows() %>%
  group_by(Variable) %>%
  mutate(p_adj_glmm = p.adjust(p_glmm, method = p_adj_method)) %>%
  ungroup()

glmm_summary <- coef_env %>%
  select(taxon_id, Variable, Estimate) %>%
  left_join(glmm_check, by = c("taxon_id", "Variable")) %>%
  transmute(taxon_id, Variable, est_glmm, p_adj_glmm,
            glmm_ok = !is.na(est_glmm) & sign(est_glmm) == sign(Estimate) & is_sig(p_glmm, p_adj_glmm))
```

## 6.5 Stability classes

```{r stability classes}
coef_stab <- coef_env
if (run_seed_check) coef_stab$seed_ok <- seed_check$coef_cor >= 0.95
if (run_loso)       coef_stab <- left_join(coef_stab, loso_summary, by = c("taxon_id", "Variable"))
if (run_lv_check)   coef_stab <- left_join(coef_stab, lv_check,     by = c("taxon_id", "Variable"))
if (run_glmm_check) coef_stab <- left_join(coef_stab, glmm_summary, by = c("taxon_id", "Variable"))

# Checks that were run
stability_checks <- intersect(c("seed_ok", "loso_ok", "lv_ok", "glmm_ok"), names(coef_stab))
coef_stab$stable_all <- if (length(stability_checks) == 0) TRUE else
  apply(as.matrix(coef_stab[, stability_checks]), 1, function(x) all(x %in% TRUE))

coef_stab <- coef_stab %>%
  mutate(stability = case_when(
    !numerically_ok | !stat_ok | !effect_ok ~ "Not supported",
    stable_all                              ~ "Robust",
    TRUE                                    ~ "Supported"),
    stability = factor(stability, levels = c("Robust", "Supported", "Not supported")))

message("Stability checks used: ", paste(stability_checks, collapse = ", "))

# How many coefficients pass each step, per predictor
stability_summary <- coef_stab %>%
  group_by(Variable) %>%
  summarise(taxa_tested       = n(),
            numerically_ok    = sum(numerically_ok),
            sig_CI_excludes_0 = sum(numerically_ok & sig_ci),
            sig_BH            = sum(numerically_ok & sig_bh),
            significant       = sum(numerically_ok & stat_ok),   # rule in sig_rule
            effect_ok         = sum(numerically_ok & stat_ok & effect_ok),
            supported         = sum(stability == "Supported"),
            robust            = sum(stability == "Robust"),
            robust_positive   = sum(stability == "Robust" & Estimate > 0),
            robust_negative   = sum(stability == "Robust" & Estimate < 0),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = names(env_vars))) %>%
  arrange(Variable)
stability_summary
```

## 6.6 Tables

```{r stability tables}
coef_export <- coef_stab %>%
  select(Phylum, Taxon = taxon, n_ASV, Variable, Estimate, SE, cilow, ciup, fold_change,
         p, p_adj, any_of(c("loso_same_sign", "loso_n", "loso_flip_site", "lv_ok",
                            "est_glmm", "p_adj_glmm", "glmm_ok")),
         stability) %>%
  mutate(across(c(Estimate, SE, cilow, ciup, fold_change, any_of("est_glmm")), ~ round(.x, 3)),
         across(c(p, p_adj, any_of("p_adj_glmm")), ~ signif(.x, 3))) %>%
  arrange(Variable, stability, Phylum, Taxon)

robust_table <- coef_export %>% filter(stability == "Robust")

save_tab(list("Stability summary per predictor" = stability_summary,
              "Robust responses"                = robust_table),
         "T4_stability_summary_robust_responses")
write.csv(coef_export, file.path(tab_dir, "T5_coefficients_all_taxa_stability.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
if (run_seed_check) save_tab(seed_check, "T6_seed_check")
```

# 7. Final coefficient plot: robust responses

Taxa with at least one robust coefficient. Only the robust coefficients are shown; panels without points mean no robust response to that predictor.

```{r final plot data}
robust_coefs <- coef_stab %>% filter(stability == "Robust")

# All coefficients of the genera with at least one robust response:
# robust ones in black, the other variables in light grey
final_df <- coef_stab %>%
  filter(taxon_id %in% robust_coefs$taxon_id, numerically_ok) %>%
  mutate(class = factor(ifelse(stability == "Robust", "Robust", "Not robust"),
                        levels = c("Robust", "Not robust")))

final_w <- 12
final_h <- max(8, 0.32 * n_distinct(robust_coefs$taxon_id) + 4)
```

```{r final plot, fig.width = final_w, fig.height = final_h}
if (nrow(robust_coefs) == 0) {
  message("No robust coefficients with the current settings.")
} else {
  # Point colours for this plot only
  class_colours_default <- class_colours
  class_colours <- c("Robust" = "black", "Not robust" = "grey75")

  final_plot <- coef_panel_plot(
    final_df,
    title     = "Reef - All Genera (Filtered by prevalence and only significant effect)",
    subtitle  = paste0("Black: robust responses (", sig_label, ", |coefficient| > log(2), stable across: ",
                       paste(sub("_ok", "", stability_checks), collapse = ", "),
                       "); grey: other coefficients of the same genera"),
    colour_by = "class", label_size = 9, x_lab = "Coefficient")
  print(final_plot)   # inside if(), a plot is only shown with print()

  save_fig(final_plot, "F8_coefficients_robust_taxa", width = final_w, height = final_h)

  class_colours <- class_colours_default   # restore for the other plots
}
```

# 8. Methods text

> Genus-level responses to the environment were assessed with generalized linear latent variable models (GLLVM; R package gllvm) fitted to filtered read counts summed per genus. ASVs without a genus assignment were grouped at their lowest assigned taxonomic rank. Taxa present in at least `r round(100 * min_prev)`% of mats and with at least `r min_reads` reads were modelled. Models used a negative binomial distribution, a random intercept for site, `r if (use_offset) "the log-transformed total number of filtered reads per mat as an offset, " else ""`and `r n_init` starting values. The number of latent variables was selected by comparing null models with 0, 1 and 2 latent variables (AIC). The environmental model included two latent variables and the standardized predictors DIN, PO₄³⁻, temperature and chlorophyll-a. Coefficients were tested with Wald tests`r if (sig_rule == "p_adj") ", and p-values were adjusted for the number of taxa tested with the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure within each predictor" else " and considered significant when the 95% confidence interval excluded zero"`. Responses were considered robust when coefficients were numerically stable (|β| < `r max_abs_est`, SE < `r max_se`), significant, represented at least a two-fold change in expected abundance per SD, and were consistent in sign across a refit from a second starting value, all leave-one-site-out refits, models with one and three latent variables, and per-taxon negative binomial GLMMs (glmmTMB).
